title: Data-driven catalyst design for direct catalytic N2O decomposition.
summary: Closed-loop ML-guided experiments identified over ten improved N2O decomposition catalysts; Rh(1)-Pd(2)/ZrO2_EP achieved the best T20 of 355°C. 633 experimental tests over 37 cycles, repeated catalytic runs, control experiments and ex situ/in situ characterization. Activity was optimized; cost and broader preparation conditions were not.
ai_technology: Extra-trees regression and human-in-the-loop candidate selection iteratively chose compositions for synthesis/testing and retrained on each experimental cycle.
organization: Institute for Catalysis, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan

evidence.ai_role: Extra-trees regression and human-in-the-loop candidate selection iteratively chose compositions for synthesis/testing and retrained on each experimental cycle.

source_review.scope: The primary ChemRxiv v1 was posted 2025-09-01 and its result is carried into the 2026 Nature Communications paper: a machine-learning/experiment closed loop ran 37 cycles and experimentally tested 633 predicted catalysts. More than ten compositions exceeded the starting best catalyst; Rh(1)-Pd(2)/ZrO2_EP reached T20=355°C versus 378°C for the initial best reference, with at least triplicate testing and ex situ/in situ mechanistic work. The optimization targeted activity, not cost. No same-reaction or same-catalyst result appears in the active or archived catalog; the existing polymerization-catalyst entry is a different reaction and material.
